messages:
Maria Chen: Quick recap from the Sec review with Acme Support earlier — they want 4 items for the questionnaire: 1) exact support access patterns (least-privilege), 2) sample audit log lines we can share, 3) how we export logs for SIEM ingest (format + pipeline), 4) proof temporary creds expire and get logged. Can someone pick up each? cc @Josh :wave:

Josh Patel: I can own the RBAC/access patterns + runbook excerpt. Is the support kube/ssh access still via ephemeral session tokens?

Maria Chen: Yes — support uses short-lived service sessions. Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/support-access (we'll extract an excerpt for the customer). They want plain language + a snippet.

Josh Patel: Ok. TL;DR for questionnaire: 
- Support roles: support-readonly, support-ops (scoped), support-impersonate (audited).
- Grant flow: engineer requests via SLA portal -> mgr approval -> one-time session token minted (STS) -> token duration 30m to 1h depending on scope.
- All actions logged to audit pipeline with actor, role, session_id.

Kevin O'Neill: I can handle the log samples + SIEM export details. Quick q: are we allowed to send real tenant IDs to Acme? I'd rather send redacted plus a signed sample.

Sara Li: Do NOT send real tenant IDs. Provide a redacted sample and the HMAC verification proof so they can verify authenticity of the sample we give. Also include our data minimization statement. :lock:

security-bot: Retention policy reminder — enterprise tier audit logs retained 365d by default; configurable during onboarding.

Kevin O'Neill: Draft sample log (redacted) below — use this in the questionnaire appendix: 

```json
{"timestamp":"2026-02-18T14:22:11Z","service":"inference-runtime","level":"INFO","event":"session.authorize","actor":"support-agent:joshuap","role":"support-impersonate","session_id":"sess-9f2a4","tenant_id":"<REDACTED>","action":"model_invocation","resource":"model-prod-v2","outcome":"success"}
```

Kevin O'Neill: SIEM export notes: we push newline-delimited JSON to S3 (gzip) and our firewall-forwarder loads to their SIEM via secure syslog or S3 pull. We can provide schema (fields + types) and a staging export.

Maria Chen: For the temporary creds proof — can we produce a short audit trace showing token mint and token expiration log lines? They want evidence that tokens expire automatically.

Josh Patel: Yes — flow: `sts:CreateSession` -> `session.issued` log -> `session.expired` log line at TTL. We'll point to the runbook and include the log snippet. Example: 

```
2026-02-18T14:21:11Z session.issued session_id=sess-9f2a4 actor=joshuap ttl=3600
2026-02-18T15:21:11Z session.expired session_id=sess-9f2a4 reason=ttl_expired
```

Sara Li: I'll draft the blurb about key management: support sessions never receive customer KEK unwrapped. KMS operations are proxied; we log KMS API calls (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) with truncated resource identifiers. Add note on HSM-backed keys for customers who opt into on-prem/private.

Kevin O'Neill: For the signed sample: we'll HMAC the sample with a verification key and provide the key fingerprint + verification steps. Example command for them to verify: 

```bash
echo -n 'sample-log-line' | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$VERIFICATION_KEY" -binary | base64
```

Maria Chen: Awesome. Action items: Josh -> collect runbook excerpt + RBAC diagram; Kevin -> redact real logs, produce signed sample + SIEM schema; Sara -> KMS/HSM blurb + policy sentence; I'll assemble questionnaire answers and send draft to legal for review. Target: EOD tomorrow.

Josh Patel: On it. I have a small RBAC diagram PNG in the runbook — can include.

Sara Li: FYI I'll add a short note about vuln triage: if a runtime CVE requires temporary escalation, we have a documented emergency ACL workflow that auto-logs approvals and recreates tokens postfix. Will include example entry.

Maria Chen: Perfect. If anything blocks, ping me. :thumbsup:
